title: Ghost in the Encoder: Decodable Artist Identity Representations in Lyrics-to-Song Generation
abstract: arXiv:2609.39552v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Text-to-song generation models can be prompted to imitate specific artists or regurgitate entire songs from their training data. Although these phenomena have been documented behaviorally on small datasets, little is known about the internal representations that may give rise to them. Prior interpretability work on generative audio has focused on locating semantic concepts such as genre or time signature within model activations. In this work, we show that a trained model can be probed for linearly decodable representations of artist identity from song lyrics alone, without any additional identifiers. Through a controlled case study of ACE-Step 1.5 spanning 2,000 songs across 100 artists, we demonstrate that the artist associated with a given set of lyrics can be identified within the model's internal activations, and that this conditioning signal propagates from the lyric encoder to the diffusion backbone during inference. translated_title: 编码器中的幽灵：歌词到歌曲生成中可解码的艺术家身份表征
translated_abstract: 文本到歌曲生成模型可以被提示去模仿特定艺术家，或从其训练数据中原样复现整首歌曲。尽管这些现象已在小规模数据集上从行为层面得到记录，但对于可能引发这些现象的内部表征却知之甚少。此前关于生成式音频的可解释性工作主要聚焦于在模型激活中定位语义概念，如音乐流派或拍号。在这项工作中，我们展示了对已训练的模型进行探测，可以仅凭歌词（无需任何额外标识符）就解码出艺术家身份的线性可解码表征。通过对ACE-Step 1.5的受控案例研究，涵盖100位艺术家的2,000首歌曲，我们证明了与给定歌词相关联的艺术家可以在模型的内部激活中被识别出来，并且这种条件信号在推理过程中会从歌词编码器传播到扩散主干网络。
tldr: 该研究首次证明仅凭歌词就能在歌词到歌曲生成模型的内部激活中线性解码出艺术家身份表征，且该信号会在推理时从歌词编码器传播至扩散主干网络，揭示了模型潜在的艺术家模仿能力来源。
en_tdlr: This study demonstrates that artist identity can be linearly decoded from lyrics alone within a lyrics-to-song generation model's internal activations, and this signal propagates from the lyric encoder to the diffusion backbone during inference.
